newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy trade min to back budget despite doubts.
newsitem.headline: Italy trade min to back budget despite doubts.

text.p: Italian Foreign Trade minister Augusto Fantozzi was quoted as saying on Friday he would back Italy's planned 62.5 trillion lire budget despite reservations over its failure to include cuts in welfare spending.

Fantozzi, who is a member of Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's Renewal party, said "the mandate from Dini was to express the dissent on the part of the Renewal party over the failure to include structural measures on health and pensions."
Fantozzi, who is in London to attend a meeting of the Italo-British chamber of commerce, was quoted by Italian news agency ANSA.
But he added he would support the budget "at a moment when the country needs to send a strong signal to the markets and also to European partners."
The government has said the 1997 budget, which includes a proposed 12.5 trillion lire "Euro-tax", will enable Italy to qualify for a European currency union by 1999.
Earlier Diego Masi announced his resignation as parliamentary leader of the Renewal party, saying the budget was made up entirely of new tax measures.
